titulo: Dative 2: verbs that take the dative: Helfen, danken, gehören

aula.titulo: Dative 2: verbs that take the dative
aula.objetivo: Use the verbs that put the person in the dative (helfen, danken, gehören, gefallen, schmecken, passen, fehlen, antworten, gratulieren, glauben) and the "how I feel" expressions with «mir» and «dir».

blocos.titulo: Verbs that take the dative: the person goes into the dative, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: some German verbs put the person in the DATIVE, even though English uses a plain direct object: «Ich helfe dir» (I help you), «Ich danke dir» (I thank you), «Das Buch gehört mir» (the book belongs to me). STEP 2: these verbs do NOT take the accusative for the person: «Ich helfe dich» is wrong, even though "help you" feels like a direct object. STEP 3: learn each verb together with «wem?»: «helfen + dative», «danken + dative», «gehören + dative». A useful trick: think "give help TO you", "give thanks TO you", "belong TO me" — the "to" is your dative. STEP 4: «helfen» changes e to i with «du» and «er» (du hilfst, er hilft). STEP 5: «gratulieren» uses «zu» + dative for the occasion: «Ich gratuliere dir zum Geburtstag» (happy birthday — literally "I congratulate to you on the birthday"). STEP 6: «antworten» takes the dative for the person and «auf» + accusative for what you're answering: «Er antwortet dem Chef auf die E-Mail» (He answers the boss's e-mail).
blocos.comparacao: English says "help him", "thank him", "answer him" with a direct object, so your instinct will say accusative (ihn). German keeps the old dative here: «Ich helfe ihm», «Ich danke ihm», «Ich antworte ihm». With «gehören», English already has the "to": "it belongs to me" = «es gehört mir».

tabela.pt: We wish you a happy birthday.

blocos.enunciado: Say 6 sentences with «helfen», «danken» and «gehören»: «Ich helfe meiner Mutter. Das Handy gehört mir.»
